title: Typing during active turn inserts red buffer error
description:
## Reproduction
1. Start a LouiseLM chat session.
2. While the model is responding / it is not the user's turn, type into the chat buffer.
3. Observe the buffer and Neovim message area.

## Observed
The chat buffer displays a red error/traceback while handling the typed input:
`vim.schedule callback: .../lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:145: replacement string item contains newlines`
The traceback points through `nvim_buf_set_lines`, `set_line`, and `handle_event`. The UI later appears normal once the turn completes (see second screenshot), but the transient error is user-visible and may indicate that streamed/event updates race with edits made while the session is active.

## Expected
Typing while it is not the user's turn should be safely rejected, queued, or otherwise handled without a red traceback or corrupted chat buffer. Any user-facing feedback should be intentional and clear.

## Evidence
- First screenshot: `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260809_0501_1920x1200_1786244489.png`
- Second screenshot: `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260809_0501_1920x1200_1786244505.png`

## Acceptance criteria
- Reproduce the issue deterministically with a mock/fast event sequence if possible.
- Identify whether the root cause is newline-containing content being passed as one `nvim_buf_set_lines` replacement item, a turn-state race, or both.
- Prevent the red traceback and preserve the intended chat content during active-turn typing.
- Add regression coverage for input arriving while streamed updates are being applied.
close_reason: Normalized multiline ACP tool titles before rendering and added regression coverage

title: Queue one next-turn chat prompt while the session is busy
description:
## Problem

Pressing Enter in the chat while the model is responding currently mutates the transcript first, then calls `Session:prompt()`. Because the session is not `ready`, the prompt is rejected and the chat records both a phantom user turn and `Error: session is not ready`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a louiselm chat session and submit a prompt that produces a response long enough to remain active.
2. While the session status is `prompting`, type another message on the chat input line and press Enter.
3. Observe that the input is appended as though it were submitted, followed by `Error: session is not ready`, even though ACP rejected the prompt.

## Expected behavior

The chat owns one pending next-turn prompt per attached session. Pressing Enter during an active turn commits the current input as that session's queued prompt. It remains outside the transcript and sends automatically only after that turn definitively completes or cancellation completes.

## Decisions

- Queue only in `prompting`, `waiting_permission`, and `cancelling`; ordinary ready-state submission remains immediate.
- Support exactly one queued prompt per session, including slash commands.
- Keep queued state with its session when switching chat buffers.
- Show `Queued for next turn` beside the input using virtual text, without modifying prompt text.
- A queued prompt is committed by Enter. Editing it returns it to draft state and requires Enter to recommit, preventing a partial edit from auto-sending.
- Snapshot attached file/selection context when the prompt is committed.
- Release the queue only at a definitive active-turn completion boundary, not on unrelated generic `ready` transitions.
- User cancellation preserves and sends the queued prompt after cancellation completes. A genuine session failure preserves it as a draft and does not send it.
- Append the user message to the transcript only after `Session:prompt()` accepts it.
- If submission fails, preserve the draft and use an editor notification; do not append an `Error:` transcript line for a prompt that was never accepted.
- During `starting` or `configuring`, Enter preserves a draft and notifies instead of queuing. Never queue in `error` or `disposed`.
- Closing a session warns explicitly that its queued prompt will be discarded. Disposal guarantees queued work cannot send later.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Enter during each active-turn state queues one prompt without adding either the prompt or an error to the transcript.
2. On normal turn completion, the committed prompt and its snapshotted context are submitted exactly once and only then appear in transcript history.
3. On completed user cancellation, the committed prompt submits exactly once; on session error it remains an unsent draft.
4. Editing a committed queued prompt makes it a draft and prevents auto-send until Enter recommits it.
5. A second queued turn cannot be accumulated; state is isolated per attached session and survives session switching.
6. Slash commands use the same queue path.
7. Startup/configuration/error/disposed states never create queued work or transcript errors from rejected input.
8. Closing/disposal clears pending work, warns when appropriate, and late scheduled events cannot submit it.
9. Add focused headless chat tests for state transitions, async scheduled event delivery, exactly-once submission, context ownership, switching, failure, cancellation, and disposal. Follow red-green-refactor and run the full required quality gates.

## Scope

- In scope: chat input/queued-prompt state, presentation, lifecycle handling, and behavioral tests.
- Out of scope: changing ACP to allow concurrent prompts, queuing multiple future turns, or changing session-core readiness rules.
close_reason: Implemented one per-session queued next-turn prompt with virtual-text state, edit invalidation, context snapshots, turn/cancellation release, rejection preservation, close/disposal safety, and README documentation. Verification: focused chat suite 27/27 passed; full mini.test suite 112/112 passed; stylua --check . passed; lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning passed with zero diagnostics; git diff --check passed.

title: Add explicit per-agent Agent Skills profiles
description:
## Problem Statement

LouiseLM currently injects one global skill index into every session, including adapters such as Codex and Claude that already provide native Agent Skills support. This exposes an implementation marker in chat, wastes context, can send a skill twice, and leaves users unable to understand which component discovers or invokes a skill.

## Solution

Add explicit per-agent Agent Skills profiles. Global skill paths remain shared, the default policy is `native`, and an agent may override only `skills.policy` with `native`, `inject`, or `off`. Native mode delegates discovery and invocation to the adapter. Inject mode provides a hidden, bounded Agent Skills catalog and attaches a selected full SKILL.md only once per activation. Off disables LouiseLM skill automation and the picker. Never infer or switch policy at runtime.

## User Stories

1. As a Codex or Claude user, I want native skills used without LouiseLM reinjecting them, so that skills are not duplicated.
2. As a custom-adapter user, I want to opt one agent into injected discovery, so that natural-language skill matching still works.
3. As a user, I want a picker that invokes a known local skill safely in both native and injected profiles, so that explicit activation is predictable.
4. As a user, I want skill context hidden before submission but inspectable afterward, so that chat stays clean without concealing what was sent.
5. As a skill author, I want malformed, shadowed, explicit-only, truncated, or inaccessible skills diagnosed clearly, so that configuration failures are understandable.
6. As a user configuring an unfamiliar ACP adapter, I want documentation explaining Agent Skills, ACP transport, host responsibilities, and filesystem assumptions, so that I can choose the correct policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Global `skills.policy` defaults to `native`; agent definitions may override only the policy, while paths remain global and session-static.
2. `native` sends no automatic catalog or skill body. Picker activation resolves against the adapter's latest advertised command list and sends exactly one advertised command plus task.
3. `inject` sends one hidden catalog only on the first accepted non-slash prompt of a new session, then sends a selected complete SKILL.md once per deliberate activation. It never falls back to native or reinjects after uncertain accepted requests.
4. `off` sends no skill automation and disables the skill picker without intercepting user-authored slash commands.
5. The old `full_content` setting and dormant automatic-native-fallback API are removed with clear migration errors and documentation.
6. Agent Skills core metadata is parsed with `lyaml` and semantically validated; Codex and Claude invocation-control extensions are recognized without treating them as ACP requirements.
7. Missing `lyaml` blocks injected sessions and local native picker/validation, but does not block native sessions themselves or off sessions.
8. The injected catalog uses the agreed Agent Skills XML shape, fixed behavioral preamble, XML escaping, and an 8,000-byte UTF-8-safe total budget with deterministic diagnostics.
9. Submitted prompt contexts are represented as one closed Neovim fold containing exact sent content in order; automatic hidden catalog text never appears as a pre-send marker.
10. README, generated configuration help/annotations, checkhealth, and migration guidance explain policy selection, no-double-send behavior, dependency installation, trust/path rules, filesystem limits, and live-only fold persistence.
11. Automated tests cover configuration, discovery, YAML, invocation metadata, native command correlation, injection lifecycle, slash deferral, failures/cancellation, no-double-send invariants, and context folds. Installed Codex/Claude checks remain documented manual smoke tests.

## Implementation Notes

- Agent Skills defines the skill format; ACP transports prompts and command updates; LouiseLM is the host responsible for policy and injected discovery.
- Explicit-only wins when `disable-model-invocation: true` or OpenAI's `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false` is present. Such skills remain picker-visible but are excluded from injected catalogs.
- Root order defines duplicate precedence; path handling is deterministic, symlink-aware, and diagnostic without adding a trust database.
- The 8,000-byte mechanism intentionally mimics Codex's conservative fallback behavior; it is not part of ACP or the Agent Skills specification.
- Use native Neovim folds and existing context transport. Do not introduce a generic fold framework.

## Testing Notes

Use MiniTest for module behavior and a mock ACP agent for command updates and prompt transport. Test public behavior and exact no-double-send invariants. Do not require authenticated live adapters in automated tests.

## Out of Scope

- Runtime policy switching or inference.
- A general UI for every ACP advertised command.
- A LouiseLM ACP filesystem service.
- Recursive embedding of skill resources.
- Persistent transcript reconstruction.
- Automatic dependency installation.
- Generic adapter-native skill implementation.
- Tool-call fold rendering; track that as a separate design question.

title: Diagnose installed lyaml outside Neovim search paths
description:
## Problem

Local skill discovery reports:

```
louiselm: lyaml is required for local skill discovery; install it with `luarocks --lua-version 5.1 install lyaml`
```

However, LuaRocks confirms that lyaml is already installed for Lua 5.1. The actual failure is that the active Neovim process does not search the LuaRocks tree, so the message sends the user toward an installation command that will not fix the search-path mismatch.

## Reproduction evidence

- `luarocks --lua-version 5.1 show lyaml` succeeds with lyaml 6.2.9-2 under `$HOME/.asdf/installs/lua/5.1.5/luarocks`.
- Neovim 0.12.2 embeds LuaJIT 2.1.
- In `nvim --headless -u NONE`, `pcall(require, "lyaml")` returns `module 'lyaml' not found`.
- Neovim's `package.path` and `package.cpath` contain system paths, but not the asdf LuaRocks share/lib paths reported by `luarocks path --lua-version 5.1`.

## Expected behavior

When lyaml cannot be loaded, LouiseLM should preserve enough of the loader failure to distinguish an absent installation from an installed-but-unreachable LuaRocks tree (and from native module load failures), then give a corrective action that matches the failure.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The user-facing/checkhealth diagnostic distinguishes at least package-not-found/search-path mismatch from a native loader failure instead of always saying to install lyaml.
2. Documentation gives a supported way to make a Lua 5.1 LuaRocks tree visible to Neovim, including non-system/asdf installs.
3. Tests cover the generic `require("lyaml")` failure mapping without depending on a real LuaRocks installation.
4. Diagnostics do not expose unrelated environment values or sensitive data.
close_reason: Shortened interactive lyaml failures to point at checkhealth, added detailed persistent zsh/asdf guidance to health and README, and covered both surfaces. Verified 181 MiniTest cases, StyLua, and LuaLS.

title: Resumed-session export silently drops nested/subagent tool calls
description:
`:LouiselmResume`'s replay of a prior ACP session silently drops nested/child
tool calls (a tool call made *by* a Task subagent, i.e. one carrying a
`parentToolUseId`), while still replaying the parent Task call's own summary
text. Anyone exporting a resumed session — including the blog publishing
pipeline, which exports whatever the agent replays on `session/load` — gets a
transcript that is missing subagent-internal tool-call detail, with no error
or signal that anything is missing.

## Observed

QA round for the transcript-export/blog-publishing features
(`4e4a58b`, `674939b`), case 4 ("resumed-session export vs live export"),
session `21a0ede3-b65e-4f1c-935d-754f22126384`, 2026-08-18.

Prompt that produced the nested call (case 1 of the same round):
"Do these three things in order, in this one turn. (1) Run the Bash tool on
the absolute path: `wc -l .../transcript.lua`. (2) Use the Task tool to
launch one general-purpose subagent whose prompt is exactly: 'List the
top-level directories of /home/lotso/code/louiselm as one comma-separated
line.' (3) Write me a two-sentence summary of what you found."

Original live export, captured right after that turn ended:
`louiselm-session-1-20260818-150448.md` (repo root at the time). Contains 3
tool-call blocks — Bash (`wc -l`), Task (`List top-level directories`), and a
nested Bash call made by the Task subagent:
```
toolCallId = "toolu_01AB1x1SdnkvcFoPF6EcmTqr"
parentToolUseId = "toolu_018NnXLu4qGQc7e4bei8C52a"  (the Task call)
title = "ls -d /home/lotso/code/louiselm/*/ | xargs -n1 basename | paste -sd, -"
rawOutput = "android,assets,blog,capture-service,configured,lua,scripts,tests"
status = "completed"
```

Resumed export (`:LouiselmResume` on the same session, immediate
`:LouiselmToMarkdown` → `/tmp/qa-resumed.md`, no other prompt sent first):
same acp session id (session/load reconnects rather than creating a new
session). Contains the parent `## Tool: List top-level directories
(completed)` block with its rawOutput summary intact, but grepping the full
573KB resumed export for the toolCallId `toolu_01AB1x1SdnkvcFoPF6EcmTqr`, the
literal command text `paste -sd`, and `xargs -n1 basename` finds zero
tool-call blocks — those strings appear exactly once, incidentally, inside
unrelated later text content (a grep-output dump quoted in a much later
turn), not as a `## Tool:` entry.

Raw jsonrpc log:
`~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260818-150022-1160867-claude-agent-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log`
(818 lines). The nested `tool_call` event for
`toolu_01AB1x1SdnkvcFoPF6EcmTqr` appears exactly once, at line 19, during the
original live turn:
```
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"session/update","params":{"sessionId":"21a0ede3-b65e-4f1c-935d-754f22126384","update":{"_meta":{"claudeCode":{"toolName":"Bash","parentToolUseId":"toolu_018NnXLu4qGQc7e4bei8C52a"}},"toolCallId":"toolu_01AB1x1SdnkvcFoPF6EcmTqr","sessionUpdate":"tool_call","rawInput":{"command":"ls -d /home/lotso/code/louiselm/*/ | xargs -n1 basename | paste -sd, -"},"status":"pending", ...}}}
```
No second occurrence appears later in the log during the replay burst
triggered by `session/load` — the agent process itself never re-emits this
event on replay.

Everything else about the resumed export checked out clean: 65 of the 66
total tool calls in the session (by then spanning many turns) present and in
correct relative order, and the case-1 `## User` block matches the typed
prompt verbatim. Only this one nested call is missing.

## Symptoms

- User sees: a resumed-session export (or a blog post built from one) that
  looks complete — full assistant text, the parent Task call's own summary —
  but is silently missing the detail of what the subagent actually did
  internally.
- System reports: nothing. No error, warning, or count mismatch anywhere;
  `Chat:to_markdown` and `create-blog.sh` both report success normally.

## Root cause

Unknown, and outside this repo (`louiselm.nvim`). `louiselm`'s own
`Transcript:record`/`Transcript.render` (lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua)
only records whatever `session/update` events it receives over ACP — the
live stream sent the nested tool_call event and louiselm recorded it
correctly (see the original export above); on replay, the same event simply
never arrives, so there is nothing to fix on this side.

Hypothesis (unverified): `claude-agent-acp`
(`/home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter`, a sibling project) or the underlying
Claude Code SDK reconstructs the Task/subagent call tree differently when
replaying a resumed session's history than when streaming it live — possibly
only replaying top-level tool calls and treating subagent-internal calls as
already-summarized by the parent's own output. Nothing in this investigation
confirms which layer (adapter vs. upstream SDK) is responsible; that needs a
look at the adapter/SDK's own session/load implementation, not louiselm's.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/session/transcript_export_spec.lua` and
`tests/session/transcript_spec.lua` exercise `Transcript` against synthetic,
hand-built event fixtures for both the live and "loaded" replay paths — no
fixture in the suite includes a nested/subagent tool call in a replay
scenario, because nobody had a real payload to model one on. This QA round
was the first time a resumed session containing a Task-subagent call was
actually exported and diffed against its own live-captured original.

## Fix direction

Not in this repo. If the root cause is confirmed to be in
`claude-agent-acp`, the fix belongs there (ensure `session/load` replay
re-emits every historical `tool_call`/`tool_call_update`, including nested
ones with `parentToolUseId` set, not just top-level calls). If it turns out
to be inherent to how the upstream Claude Code SDK exposes subagent history
on resume, this may not be fixable without a scope change to what
`session/load` guarantees — in which case the practical mitigation is
documentation: warn blog-pipeline users that `create-blog.sh` on a resumed
session may omit subagent-internal tool-call detail, and recommend exporting
live when that detail matters.

## Acceptance

- A regression test in whichever repo owns the fix: replay a session
  containing a Task call with a nested tool call, and assert the replayed
  event stream includes the nested `tool_call`/`tool_call_update` events,
  not just the parent's.
- Re-run this round's case 4 comparison
  (`louiselm-session-1-20260818-150448.md` vs. a fresh `:LouiselmResume` +
  immediate `:LouiselmToMarkdown` export of the same session) and confirm
  `toolu_01AB1x1SdnkvcFoPF6EcmTqr` (or an equivalent nested call in a new
  repro) is present in the resumed export.

## Not covered

- Which of `claude-agent-acp` vs. the upstream Claude Code SDK is actually
  responsible — unverified, needs investigation in that repo, not this one.
- Whether the same gap exists for other nested-call shapes (e.g. a tool call
  made by a tool call, rather than by a Task subagent specifically) — only
  one nested-call example existed in the session under test.
- Whether `create-blog.sh` (case 5, not yet run at time of filing) actually
  reproduces the same gap end-to-end through the headless path — this bug is
  filed from the interactive `:LouiselmResume` path only; case 5 should
  re-check this once it runs.

title: Stack LouieLM transcript content in chronological order
description:
## Problem

In the latest screenshot of a LouieLM session, the transcript content feels split by type: the conversation text appears above while tool activity/status lines are grouped at the bottom near the prompt. This makes the sequence of the session awkward to follow.

## Desired behavior

Render each printed item in one chronological vertical stack, including model text, user text, tool calls, tool results, and status messages. New items should appear after the preceding item in the same transcript flow, with the composer/input area remaining at the bottom.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Model text, user text, tool activity, tool results, and status messages appear in a single chronological transcript order.
2. Tool output is positioned next to or directly after the event that produced it rather than in a separate bottom group.
3. The input/composer remains clearly separated from transcript history at the bottom.
4. Existing session header and chat behavior remain unchanged.

Source report: /tmp/nvim-wtu.md

title: LouiselmToMarkdown crashes with uncaught E482 instead of a clean write error
description:
`:LouiselmToMarkdown` crashes with an uncaught Lua/Vimscript error instead of
the clean "could not write markdown file: ..." message when the destination's
parent directory does not exist.

## Observed

Manual QA round on commits 674939b (blog publishing pipeline) and 4e4a58b
(session transcript export), case 2.2/2.3 in QA_REVIEW.md. User ran
`:LouiselmToMarkdown`, typed `~/tmp/qa-export.md` (nonexistent dir):

```
louiselm markdown path (blank for default): ~/tmp/qa-export.md
Lua :command callback: Vim:E482
: Can't open file ~/tmp/qa-export.md for writing: no such file or directory
stack traceback:
        [C]: in function 'writefile'
        ...ack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1561: in function 'to_markdown'
        .../core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:276: in function 'on_confirm'
        ...installs/neovim/0.12.2/share/nvim/runtime/lua/vim/ui.lua:114: in function 'input'
        .../core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:272: in function <.../core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:266>
```

Reproduced identically with the absolute path `/tmp/nope/qa-export.md`
(missing dir), ruling out `~`-expansion as the sole cause — the real trigger
is any nonexistent parent directory.

## Symptoms

- User sees a raw `E482` Lua stack trace in `:messages`, not a `louiselm:`
  notification.
- The chat UI's own error path (`report_error`) never fires for this failure.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1561`:

```lua
if nvim.fn.writefile(split_lines(markdown), destination) ~= 0 then
  return nil, "could not write markdown file: " .. destination
end
```

This assumes `writefile()` reports failure via a nonzero return. In Neovim,
when the destination cannot be opened at all (missing parent directory, no
permission), `writefile()` throws `E482` as a Lua error instead of returning
a value — so the `~= 0` check is dead code for this failure mode and the
error propagates uncaught through `Chat:to_markdown` ->
`command.lua:276 on_confirm` -> `vim.ui.input`.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua` covers the success path, "no chat
session", "not attached", and "disposed" errors, but has no case where
`writefile` itself fails (e.g. destination inside a nonexistent directory).
The suite never exercises the real `writefile()` call against an unwritable
path.

## Fix direction

Wrap the `writefile` call in `pcall` in `Chat:to_markdown` (init.lua:1561) so
any thrown error is caught and converted into the existing
`"could not write markdown file: " .. destination` return.

## Acceptance

- A regression test in tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua that calls
  `to_markdown` with a path inside a nonexistent directory and asserts a
  clean `(nil, "could not write markdown file: " .. path)` return with no
  thrown error.
- Manually confirmed: `:LouiselmToMarkdown` against a missing directory shows
  a `louiselm: could not write markdown file: ...` notification, no stack
  trace in `:messages`.

## Not covered

`~` is not expanded by `vim.fn.writefile` either (a second, separate
usability issue: paths starting with `~` will still fail even inside an
existing directory tree, just with a clean error now instead of a crash).
Not filing separately since the pcall fix already turns it into the correct
clean-error path; only worth a follow-up if users expect `~` to expand.
close_reason: Fixed in 6167df0. Root cause: nvim.fn.writefile throws E482 (Lua error) instead of returning nonzero when the destination directory doesn't exist, so Chat:to_markdown's `~= 0` check never caught the failure. Fix: wrapped the writefile call in pcall (init.lua:1561), converting any thrown error into the existing clean 'could not write markdown file: ...' return. Tests: added 'reports a clean error instead of crashing when the destination directory does not exist' to tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua -- failed with the exact E482 traceback before the fix, passes after. Gates: full mini.test suite (235/235 cases) and stylua --check on both changed files pass. No deviation from filed acceptance criteria.

title: Open every UI selector outside insert mode
description:
## Problem

Commit 1eb309a fixed permission selection by leaving insert mode immediately before vim.ui.select. That diagnosis is correct: Chat:attach enters insert mode, and list-focused select providers can otherwise receive the wrong mode and confirm or edit the wrong picker state.

The same bug remains in session configuration. Chat:attach schedules open_session_options after entering insert mode, while both the options overview and its nested model/value picker call vim.ui.select without normalizing mode. This affects the automatic first-session overview and can also affect :LouiselmSessionOptions when invoked from an insert-mode mapping.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Attach a ready session that advertises a model or boolean configuration option.
2. Let Chat:attach focus the prompt and enter insert mode.
3. Wait for the scheduled initial options overview, or invoke :LouiselmSessionOptions from an insert-mode mapping.
4. Observe that vim.ui.select is called while the inherited mode is insert; with a list-focused provider, navigation or confirmation targets the wrong picker state.
5. Select an option such as Model and observe the nested value picker has the same unnormalized boundary.

## Investigation

There are 12 vim.ui.select call sites across chat, context, and diff UI. In addition to session options, selectors that are asynchronous, nested, or exposed through public Chat methods can inherit insert mode: resumed-session selection, remembered-permission selection and confirmation, session switch/close, agent selection, and file/skill context selection. The permission picker is now protected. The diff-review selector is currently protected indirectly because the focused diff buffer exits insert mode before its normal-mode actions run.

## Scope

- Normalize mode at the narrowest shared LouiseLM selection boundary immediately before opening every vim.ui.select picker.
- Cover both stages of the session-options flow, especially the model/value picker opened by :LouiselmSessionOptions and the automatic picker scheduled by Chat:attach.
- Migrate or audit every raw vim.ui.select call in lua/louiselm/ui so no insert-mode-sensitive sibling remains.
- Preserve provider ownership of picker layout and interaction; do not detect or configure Snacks or another provider.
- Preserve selection values, cancellation behavior, asynchronous scheduling, and disposal guards.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The automatically opened session-options overview is invoked outside insert mode after Chat:attach starts the prompt in insert mode.
2. The nested model/boolean value picker is also invoked outside insert mode.
3. Every LouiseLM vim.ui.select call either uses the shared normalization boundary or has a tested invariant proving insert mode cannot reach it.
4. The existing permission-picker mode regression remains green, and diff review remains in normal mode.
5. Headless behavioral tests cover the session-options regression and at least one representative shared/public or asynchronous selector path without relying on provider internals.
6. The focused UI tests, full MiniTest suite, StyLua check, and lua-language-server check pass.
close_reason: Normalized all 12 vim.ui.select call sites through one normal-mode picker boundary. Added red-green regressions for automatic/nested session options and file context selection. Verification: focused chat 44/44, context 5/5, diff 5/5; full MiniTest 185/185; StyLua and LuaLS passed; git diff --check passed.

title: Keep the chat header compact instead of dumping session metadata
description:
## Problem

The chat buffer header expands into a long Markdown heading containing every session option and context field. At normal split widths it wraps across visual rows, dominates the top of the conversation, and is difficult to scan.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a chat session whose agent reports several configuration options plus context or cost telemetry.
2. Display the chat in a typical narrow vertical split.
3. Observe that the level-one Markdown heading includes all metadata and wraps across multiple visual rows.

## Observed

A Codex session currently renders a heading such as:

`# codex · session-1 · ready · Mode=agent-full-access · Collaboration mode=default · Model=gpt-5.6-sol · Reasoning effort=xhigh · Fast mode=off · context=62585/258400 (24% normal) · Your turn`

The screenshot `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260809_0534_1920x1200_1786246460.png` shows this heading wrapping in the chat split.

## Expected

The transcript heading remains a compact, stable summary of session identity and current turn state, for example `# codex · session-1 · ready · Your turn`. Detailed configuration and telemetry remain discoverable through session options or a separate secondary status surface instead of being concatenated into an unbounded Markdown heading.

## Likely Root Cause

`session_summary()` appends every `config_options` entry plus context and cost telemetry, and `session_header()` uses the complete summary as the level-one Markdown heading. The heading length therefore scales with agent capabilities and enabled metadata.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The level-one chat heading contains only concise session identity/lifecycle/turn information and stays readable at a typical vertical split width.
2. Static/default fields such as mode, collaboration mode, model, reasoning effort, and fast mode are not dumped into the transcript heading.
3. Detailed configuration remains accessible through the existing session-options flow or another clearly defined secondary surface; do not silently remove the ability to inspect or change supported options.
4. Useful dynamic telemetry such as context pressure or cost, if retained in the UI, is presented outside the primary Markdown heading and does not make that heading grow without bound.
5. Header updates for state changes, renamed sessions, loaded sessions, and turn transitions continue to work.
6. Add or update headless UI behavior tests using a session with several config options and context telemetry. Assert the compact buffer heading and continued access to configuration; use a manual narrow-split smoke check for wrapping rather than a pixel assertion.

## Scope

- In scope: chat header/status presentation and its behavioral tests.
- Out of scope: changing ACP session metadata, removing configuration controls, or redesigning the rest of the transcript.
close_reason: Split compact session identity from the detailed switcher summary so chat headings contain only name/agent/id/lifecycle/turn while options and telemetry remain accessible. Verification: focused chat suite 27/27 passed; full mini.test suite 112/112 passed; stylua --check . passed; lua-language-server reported zero diagnostics; 48-column headless smoke passed; git diff --check passed.

title: LouiselmToMarkdown prompts for a path before validating an explicit session id
description:
`:LouiselmToMarkdown <session_id>` prompts for a destination path before
checking whether `<session_id>` is actually attached, so an invalid id wastes
a full path-entry interaction before failing.

## Observed

Manual QA round on commits 674939b/4e4a58b, case 2.4 in QA_REVIEW.md. User
ran `:LouiselmToMarkdown not-a-session-id`, was shown the
"louiselm markdown path (blank for default):" prompt, typed a path, and only
then got the `louiselm: session is not attached` error. Expected (and every
other id-consuming failure in this command family gives) an immediate error
with no interactive prompt in between.

## Symptoms

- User types and confirms a file path for an export that was never going to
  happen.
- No data loss or crash — the eventual error message is correct — but the
  ordering is surprising and wastes an interaction.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:266-282`:

```lua
nvim.api.nvim_create_user_command("LouiselmToMarkdown", function(arguments)
  ...
  local session_id = arguments.args ~= "" and arguments.args or nil
  nvim.ui.input({ prompt = "louiselm markdown path (blank for default): " }, function(path)
    ...
    local written_path, write_error = chat:to_markdown(session_id, path ~= "" and path or nil)
    ...
```

The session-id validity check lives inside `Chat:to_markdown`
(`init.lua:1553-1557`), which only runs after `vim.ui.input`'s callback
fires. `command.lua` has no way to check `session_id` validity up front
without reaching into `Chat`'s private `self.views` table.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua` covers "not attached" at the
`Chat:to_markdown` level directly (bypassing the command layer), and
`tests/ui/command_spec.lua` stubs `vim.ui.input` so it never observes prompt
ordering relative to session validation. No test exercises the command's
real `vim.ui.input` flow with a bad session id end to end.

## Fix direction

Add a small public predicate, e.g. `Chat:is_attached(session_id)` (mirroring
the existing inline check in `Chat:switch`, init.lua:1444-1461), and have
`LouiselmToMarkdown` call it before opening the `vim.ui.input` prompt when an
explicit session id was given, reporting the error immediately instead.

Deliberately not fixing in the same pass as louiselm-dim, to keep that fix's
batch to the one crash bug; this is UX ordering, not a crash.

## Acceptance

- A test (likely in tests/ui/command_spec.lua, alongside its existing
  `vim.ui.input` stub) asserting that `:LouiselmToMarkdown <bad-id>` reports
  "session is not attached" without ever invoking the input prompt.
- Manually confirmed: `:LouiselmToMarkdown not-a-session-id` shows the error
  immediately, no path prompt.

## Not covered

Whether other future id-taking commands should share this predicate — only
`LouiselmToMarkdown` takes a raw typed session id today.

title: Grill-me needed: how should qa-review rounds be archived, and does beads belong in the loop
description:
Not actionable as-is — this is a seed for a future grill-me session, not a
spec to implement from. Surfaced at the close of the transcript-export/
blog-publishing QA round (2026-08-18), when a process question came up that
didn't fit anywhere in the existing skill chain.

## The open questions

- **Archiving authority.** Once a qa-review round closes, does the working
  file (`QA_REVIEW.md`-style) become the durable record of what was tested
  and found, or is it disposable scratch once findings are filed to beads?
  Right now nothing says either way, so rounds just accumulate as loose
  untracked files.
- **Where archiving sits in the qa-review process.** Should the qa-review
  skill itself have a defined "closing" step that decides what happens to
  the file (commit it, summarize it into beads, delete it), or is that
  always a manual call by whoever's running the round?
- **Could beads be leveraged more directly.** Instead of (or alongside) a
  markdown working file, could a qa-review round's cases/results live in
  beads itself — e.g. as a parent issue with the plan, sub-issues per case?
  Unclear if that's better or just adds ceremony to something that works
  fine as a file today.

## Why this doesn't fit the usual chain

Their standing workflow is grill-me -> to-beads -> tasks executed across
sessions ("skill chaining"). Within a qa-review round, a code bug correctly
triggers to-beads-bug — that chain already works. But this round produced a
different kind of finding: not a bug, a question about the skills/workflow
itself. There's currently no formalized way for a skill to route that kind
of self-reflective finding anywhere — it only survived this time because the
user happened to notice and say it was worth a grill-me session. Whether
findings like this should sometimes get folded directly into a skill's own
instructions (when concrete enough) versus always deferred to a grill-me
session (when still vague) is itself part of what's open here.

## A concrete proposal already on record

This question isn't new — the user raised it explicitly at the *start* of
this same QA round, in an earlier session (`claude/85f97534-8fa6-4d95-a05a-7c0851bec937`):
"while we do this i want you to think if those reviews conversation or
document you produce as part of the review could leverage beads for
historical / archiving purposes." That session's assistant answered with a
concrete sketch the user liked and wants preserved verbatim here for the
grill-me session to react to, not re-derive:

1. **One bead per round**, type `chore`, label `qa-round`, created with
   `--description-file QA_REVIEW.md`. The whole plan lands in
   `.beads/issues.jsonl`, which is committed — so the round becomes
   greppable history instead of an untracked file you have to decide about
   at the end. That's the exact question that ended the *previous* round
   (the permissions round) unresolved too: "commit it as a record, or
   delete it."
2. **Findings hang off it as children.** `br create -t bug --parent
   <round-id>` — the graph then answers "which round found this?" and `br
   graph` shows a round's blast radius. This round's findings
   (`louiselm-dim`, `louiselm-euj`, `louiselm-d2o`, `louiselm-xrf`) are
   already beads but orphaned from the round that produced them — exactly
   the gap this proposal closes.
3. **Round-by-round narration goes in `br comments add`** — append-only and
   timestamped, matching the loop shape (plan, run, learn, edit). The
   markdown file stays the live scratchpad *during* the round since it
   churns every round; beads takes the final state on close.
4. **`--external-ref` holds the session id** (e.g.
   `claude/21a0ede3-b65e-4f1c-935d-754f22126384` for this round), which
   dovetails with the user's global commit-message rule (`Refs <id>` for
   named sessions/issues), and `br orphans` catches anything referenced in a
   commit but still open.

The convergence the prior session flagged as the nice part: the
transcript-export feature this very round was testing turns a session into
a publishable artifact. So under this proposal the bead becomes the index,
the exported transcript is the evidence, and a blog post (via the same
publishing pipeline, once `louiselm-xrf` is fixed) is the human-readable
version of the same round — three layers of the same feature set reused for
QA's own record-keeping instead of a fourth bespoke mechanism.

## Bigger context

Connects to a broader, previously-discussed wish: the user's own workflow
(grill-me/beads/session-chaining) eventually being expressible as a
configurable part of louiselm itself, not just a convention they follow by
hand. Not fully re-litigated here — worth pulling that thread in the
grill-me session too.

## Not covered

No decision on the concrete proposal above — it was well-received when
sketched, but never evaluated against the three open questions or actually
tried on a round (this round still used a plain `QA_REVIEW.md`). Left for
the grill-me session: whether to adopt it as-is, adapt it, or reject it in
favor of something else.

title: Recover and resume ACP sessions
description:
## Problem Statement

Recovering an existing ACP conversation currently requires users to know the adapter name, exact ACP session ID, adapter configuration, and working directory, then execute Lua manually. Normal users need a discoverable resume flow without losing the current chat.

## Solution

Add a `:LouiseLmResume` flow that discovers recoverable sessions from configured ACP adapters, filters them to the current workspace by default, and loads the selected session into a separate chat buffer. Keep the public Lua load API as the underlying and advanced recovery path.

## User Stories

1. As a user, I want to pick a prior session from a list so I can continue work without remembering opaque ACP IDs.
2. As a user, I want the default list limited to the current workspace so unrelated sessions do not overwhelm me.
3. As a user, I want an explicit all-workspaces view so older sessions remain recoverable.
4. As a user, I want resuming to preserve my current chat and open the recovered conversation separately.
5. As a user, I want load failures explained without silently creating a new session.
6. As an advanced user, I want the Lua `load_session` API to remain available.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given configured adapters that support session listing, the resume flow lists sessions with available adapter, workspace, display name, and activity metadata.
2. Given the default resume view, only sessions for the current workspace are shown; an explicit action reveals other workspaces.
3. Given a selected session, louiselm uses the current configured adapter definition and ACP `session/load`, then attaches it to a new chat buffer.
4. Given an existing attached chat, resuming does not replace or dispose it.
5. Given a missing, unsupported, or failed session load, the UI reports the specific failure and does not create a replacement session.
6. Given a loaded session, ACP-replayed history appears in the new chat before it is marked ready.
7. Given a session adapter cannot list sessions, exact-ID loading remains available through the public Lua API.
8. A lightweight local cache may accelerate discovery, but the ACP adapter remains authoritative; stale entries are handled as load failures and can be removed.
9. Session identity is scoped by adapter, ACP session ID, and workspace; old adapter commands are never reused.

## Implementation Notes

- Build on the existing session registry/API and chat attach lifecycle.
- Add ACP session-list support only where advertised; preserve graceful fallback for adapters without it.
- Keep discovery/cache state separate from conversation history.
- Use the existing asynchronous callback/event model and test production scheduling boundaries.

## Testing Notes

- Test listing/filtering and stable session identity across adapters and workspaces.
- Test successful load/replay/attach without disturbing an existing chat.
- Test unsupported listing, missing sessions, adapter failures, and no silent new-session fallback.
- Test the public Lua load path remains functional.

## Out of Scope

- Changing ACP persistence semantics or adapter storage.
- Reusing historical adapter commands.
- Automatically deleting adapter-side sessions.
- Reconstructing conversation history from louiselm cache data.
close_reason: Implemented discoverable ACP session resume flow; all 125 tests, StyLua, LuaLS, and diff check pass.

Updated the mock ACP agent and README. Verification: focused red-green tests, full mini.test suite 125/125, stylua --check ., lua-language-server zero diagnostics, and git diff --check all pass.

title: Permission evaluation calls sha256 in fast event
description:
## Reproduction

During an ACP command permission request, LouiseLM errors in the callback with:

`E5560: Vimscript function "sha256" must not be called in a fast event context`

Screenshot: ~/Pictures/scrot/20260815_1140_1920x1200_1786786845.png

## Cause

`lua/louiselm/permission/store.lua:176` calls `vim.fn.sha256()` from `Store:evaluate()`. ACP stdout/message handling runs in a fast event callback, and remembered-rule validation reaches `rule_id()` while reading permission state.

## Expected

Permission requests are evaluated and displayed without violating Neovim fast-event restrictions.

## Acceptance

- Add regression coverage for evaluating a persisted permission rule from a fast-event-like callback.
- Remove the `vim.fn.sha256()` fast-event violation without adding a dependency.
- Permission requests continue to fail closed on malformed state.
- Focused and full test suites pass.
close_reason: Fixed by deferring ACP agent request callbacks out of Neovim fast-event context in acp/init.lua; added regression coverage. Verification: focused ACP tests, full MiniTest suite (182 cases), stylua --check ., and lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning pass.

title: blog/scripts/create-blog.sh: scaffold a post, optional session auto-export
description:
## Goal
One script that scaffolds a new blog post directory, and — when given session ids — also exports each named session into it and stubs a literalinclude block per session.

## Scope
- In scope: blog/scripts/create-blog.sh <name> [session-id...]. Bare mode creates blog/post-<name>/{blog.md, conversations/} (blog.md empty, conversations/ empty). Session-id mode additionally exports each session into conversations/<session-id>.md via the same export path LouiselmToMarkdown uses (e.g. by driving headless Neovim to run that command), and appends one literalinclude block per session to blog.md pointing at ./conversations/<session-id>.md with a placeholder :lines: value.
- Out of scope: rendering excerpts through Neovim/Catppuccin (that is the render-post.sh task), MyST site config, choosing real line ranges (author does that by hand afterward).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Given create-blog.sh <name> with no session ids: blog/post-<name>/blog.md (empty) and blog/post-<name>/conversations/ (empty dir) exist.
2. Given create-blog.sh <name> <session-id>...: the same scaffold exists, plus conversations/<session-id>.md for each session id (non-empty, matching LouiselmToMarkdown's output for that session), plus blog.md containing one literalinclude block per session id referencing ./conversations/<session-id>.md.
3. Running the script twice with the same name does not silently clobber an existing post directory (errors or requires an explicit flag).

## Testing
- Script-level test: given a fake/stubbed session export, assert the created directory structure and blog.md contents match expectations.
- No Neovim UI testing needed — this is a shell script invoking headless Neovim, testable by stubbing that invocation.

## Notes
- Depends on LouiselmToMarkdown existing (task above) for the session-id auto-export path — the bare-mode scaffold alone has no dependency, but this task ships both modes together since they are one script.
- Not a Neovim command; intentionally not part of the plugin's discoverable command surface (blog/scripts/, not lua/louiselm/).
- Parent feature: louiselm-r1k.

title: Render persistent telemetry and grouped session diagnostics
description:
## Goal

Keep live, actionable session telemetry visible throughout long conversations while preserving a complete, copyable diagnostic block at the top of the chat transcript. Preserve adapter-provided values quasi as-is and make ACP versus LouiseLM-derived information visually distinguishable for QA.

## Reference

The motivating session rendered one long wrapped heading containing the ACP report id, local session id, lifecycle state, skills state, five adapter options, context usage, and turn label. Screenshot: /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260816_0632_948x1084_1786854748.png.

This task supersedes the design scope left after louiselm-kuc, whose persistent turn label was already implemented by commit 106aa9c. It builds on the completed compact-header work in louiselm-dv9 without reopening that historical task.

## Persistent Winbar Contract

Use the existing window-local winbar as the single persistent surface. Render fields in this order when available:

    Your turn · context=148222/258400 (57%) · cost=1.5 USD

- Keep the existing friendly lifecycle labels: Your turn, Model responding, Waiting for permission, Stopping, Starting, Error, and Unavailable.
- Give lifecycle states semantic ready/active/warning/error styling; semantic urgency takes precedence over provenance styling.
- Render adapter-reported context used/size quasi as-is with ACP provenance styling.
- Render only the LouiseLM-derived percentage in parentheses with derived provenance styling. Do not display the normal/elevated/high/critical pressure taxonomy.
- After a model change, retain the last context reading and append an explicit derived stale marker until a fresh adapter usage update arrives.
- Render cumulative cost quasi as-is only after the adapter reports it. Retain the last reported cumulative cost when later usage updates omit cost; remove it when the adapter explicitly clears it. Never invent zero, unknown, or unsupported placeholders.
- If context or cost has never been reported, omit that segment.
- Do not include session identity, model, mode, adapter options, or tool activity in the winbar. Tool activity remains in chronological transcript messages.
- Keep all telemetry on this one surface. Do not add a statusline, tabline, floating HUD, or pinned split.

## Transcript Diagnostic Contract

Replace the single unbounded heading with one contiguous, complete block using one compact logical line per category:

    # codex/ACP_SESSION_ID · session-1
    Session: status=ready · display=Your turn · skills=native
    ACP options: Mode=agent · Collaboration mode=default · Model=gpt-5.6-sol · Reasoning effort=xhigh · Fast mode=off
    Telemetry: context=148222/258400 (57%) · cost=1.5 USD

- Keep the full ACP report identity and local session identity in the first line.
- Preserve both raw LouiseLM lifecycle status and its friendly display label so copied QA evidence exposes their mapping.
- Show the exact skills policy: native, inject, or off. Do not collapse native and inject into on.
- Preserve adapter option names, typed current values, and adapter order on one compact logical line. Allow normal Neovim wrapping; do not add width-dependent packing or one-option-per-line rendering.
- Deliberately duplicate context and cost in the diagnostic block and winbar. The winbar is the live HUD; the transcript block is the complete copyable snapshot. Both must render from the same session state and formatting logic so they cannot disagree.
- Keep the block current when lifecycle state, configuration options, context, cost, or stale state changes.

## Provenance and Rendering

- Use explicit section labels as the primary provenance signal: Session for LouiseLM state and ACP options for adapter configuration. These labels survive copying.
- In mixed telemetry, use named user-overridable highlight groups for ACP values and LouiseLM-derived values. Do not hard-code colors.
- Keep textual structure sufficient without color: raw counts remain separate from parenthesized percentage/stale annotations.
- Escape statusline syntax in all dynamic winbar segments before composing highlight directives. Adapter-originated text must not be able to alter winbar formatting.
- Do not let provenance coloring weaken semantic error or permission states.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Scrolling a long chat keeps the friendly lifecycle label, exact reported context counts, derived percentage, stale validity, and optional last-reported cost visible in the window-local winbar.
2. Adapters that omit context or cost produce no fabricated values or placeholders, and explicit cost clearing removes the persistent cost.
3. Context pressure words are absent from both persistent and diagnostic displays; the derived percentage remains.
4. The transcript starts with the four logical diagnostic categories above, remains contiguous and copyable, uses exact skills policy and ACP option order, and intentionally duplicates live telemetry.
5. Raw status and friendly display label update together for every lifecycle state. Header and winbar telemetry cannot diverge because they share canonical formatting.
6. Provenance remains understandable without color and is additionally visible through user-overridable highlight groups; dynamic winbar content is statusline-escaped.
7. Existing winbar save/restore, session switching, disposal, scheduling, and late-event safety remain intact.
8. Headless tests cover lifecycle changes, context and cost updates/omission/clearing, model-change staleness, exact skills policies, several ACP options, provenance highlights, statusline escaping, and restoration. Include a manual narrow-split smoke check rather than width-specific pixel assertions.

title: Answering a diff review no longer returns to the previous buffer
description:
Regression introduced by the BufWipeout handler in 0ed18d0. Accepting or rejecting a review left the user in whatever buffer Neovim picked after the wipe instead of the chat.

clear() in lua/louiselm/ui/diff/init.lua read self.previous_buffer AFTER calling Buffer.close(buffer). nvim_buf_delete runs BufWipeout synchronously, and that handler clears every field including previous_buffer, so clear() then saw nil and skipped nvim_set_current_buf.

Found by manual QA (case 3, session ade1d689-6c62-4753-ad00-4c78c995b1ef): the edit was allowed and applied correctly, but the chat buffer never came back.

## Goal
A batch script that renders every literalinclude block tagged :class: nvim-transcript in a finished post through the author's real Neovim config into namespaced HTML fragments, so the blog theme and the Neovim theme cannot collide on the same page.

## Scope
- In scope: blog/scripts/render-post.sh <post-dir>. Parses blog.md for code blocks tagged nvim-transcript, extracts the referenced source file + :lines: range for each, opens the author's real Neovim config headlessly (not nvim --clean) once for the whole batch, renders each excerpt (via TOhtml / tohtml.tohtml()), extracts only the <pre> fragment and generated CSS from each, namespaces every generated selector under a wrapper class, deduplicates the CSS into one shared stylesheet file, writes fragment HTML files into the post directory.
- Out of scope: any MyST build-time plugin (rendering is a separate, explicit, pre-build step by design — not invoked from myst build/myst start); any interactive/visual-selection preview UX (explicitly rejected — plain Neovim navigation is how line ranges get picked).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Given a blog.md with one or more nvim-transcript-tagged blocks, running the script produces one HTML fragment per block and one shared namespaced CSS file.
2. Generated CSS selectors are scoped under a wrapper class (e.g. .Comment becomes .nvim-transcript .Comment) — verified selectors cannot affect anything outside that wrapper.
3. Running the script twice against unchanged input is idempotent: byte-identical output both times.
4. The author's actual Neovim config (Catppuccin colorscheme, Tree-sitter highlighting) is what produces the rendering — not a generic/default Neovim config.

## Testing
- Focused test on the CSS-namespacing step: given sample TOhtml output, assert every generated selector is correctly prefixed.
- Idempotency test: run twice against the same fixture post, diff the outputs, assert no difference.
- No UI/buffer testing needed — headless tooling only.

## Notes
- Flagged in the parent feature as the highest-risk piece of this decomposition — may reasonably exceed typical task size given TOhtml extraction, CSS parsing/rewriting, and batch orchestration are all part of one coherent capability.

title: Separate the first assistant output from the user blockquote
description:
## Problem
The first assistant output after a submitted prompt is not visually separated from the user turn and can inherit the pink Markdown blockquote styling. This makes the first commentary and following tool-call line look like part of the user message.

## Reproduction
1. Open a LouiseLM chat buffer and submit a prompt.
2. Have the agent emit a text chunk as its first event, followed by a tool call.
3. Observe the boundary between the final line of the `> ` user prompt and the initial assistant commentary/tool timeline.

## Observed
- The initial assistant commentary begins immediately below the user prompt with no blank separator.
- The first tool-call line follows inside the same visually pink region.
- In `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260809_0534_1920x1200_1786246460.png`, lines 4 onward initially appear attached to the user turn and inherit its pink presentation.

## Expected
Every assistant turn begins as a visually distinct transcript block. Assistant commentary and tool-call lines must not inherit the user prompt blockquote styling, regardless of which event arrives first.

## Likely Root Cause
`Chat:submit()` creates a single empty response placeholder immediately after the `> ` prompt. The first `chunk` event replaces that placeholder with response text instead of preserving a blank turn separator. With the chat buffer using Markdown filetype, text directly following a blockquote can be parsed as a lazy continuation, so the initial assistant content and adjacent tool-call lines inherit the blockquote highlight. This is a rendering-boundary issue; do not special-case tool colors unless investigation disproves it.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A blank separator remains between each submitted user blockquote and the first assistant transcript content.
2. Initial assistant text and tool-call lines render outside the user blockquote/pink region.
3. The boundary is correct when the first event is a text chunk, tool call, error, or other transcript-producing event.
4. Streaming multiple chunks and updating a started tool call in place do not accumulate extra blank lines or disturb chronological order.
5. Existing prompt placement, cursor behavior, and subsequent-turn rendering remain unchanged.
6. Add a headless behavioral regression test that asserts the buffer lines for a submitted prompt followed by asynchronously scheduled chunk and tool events; exercise the real scheduling boundary rather than only invoking the renderer synchronously.

## Notes
Fix the shared transcript/turn boundary rather than applying presentation logic to one tool-call event. Buffer-line behavior is the primary assertion; no pixel test is required.

title: Resumed sessions drop the user's own messages from the transcript
description:
After :LouiselmResume the chat shows the agent replies and tool calls from the prior conversation but none of the user prompts, so a resumed session reads as one-sided and anything the user wrote — a session id, a decision, a constraint — is invisible.

## Observed

Session claude/fa72dc03-6c22-41c8-be19-9274bea75695, resumed 2026-08-17 08:50.

~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260817-085040-286753-claude-agent-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log replays both prompts before the session/load result:

  line 1  user_message_chunk  "commit and sync, those skills addition have been performed in claude/71c82ed5-9db8-44a3-9e64-e610a51b6cea"
  line 24 user_message_chunk  "sorry redo it i miscliked"
  line 37 session result for fa72dc03-6c22-41c8-be19-9274bea75695

Neither line appeared in the resumed chat buffer. The text is intact in ~/.claude/projects/-home-lotso-dotfiles-nvim--config-nvim/fa72dc03-....jsonl, so nothing is lost upstream; only the client drops it.

## Root cause

lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua handle_notification dispatches update types at lines 184-209: agent_message_chunk, tool_call, tool_call_update, config_option_update, usage_update. user_message_chunk matches nothing and falls through silently.

claude-agent-acp is launched with --replay-user-messages, so the replay is expected behavior of the agent, not a quirk.

## Why it was not caught

tests/ui/chat_spec.lua "renders replayed assistant chunks before a new prompt" covers the resume path but only asserts the agent side, so the missing half of the conversation is invisible to it.

## Fix direction

Handle user_message_chunk and render it as a user prompt line in the transcript.

Check whether the chunk arrives outside replay before deciding where to render. Evidence so far: across every stored adapter log, user_message_chunk appears only in logs that include a session/load replay - claude, codex and the deepseek adapter all behave this way, and live turns in the same logs never emit it. If an agent does echo the prompt during a live turn, the chat would double-render it, because the chat writes the submitted prompt into the buffer itself.

## Acceptance

- A resumed session shows the user prompts interleaved with the agent replies in their original order.
- Submitting a prompt in a live turn still renders it exactly once.
- A chat_spec case asserts a replayed user chunk reaches the buffer.

## Not covered

Whether replayed prompts should be visually distinguished from newly typed ones, and whether replayed tool calls should be folded, are UX questions left open.

title: LouiseLM attention control plane: ideas into reality
description:
## Problem Statement

Ideas arrive faster than sustained human attention can evaluate and realize them. Existing agent tools automate isolated conversations and coding turns but do not make the whole workflow, its authority boundaries, or its human-attention gates observable.

## Solution

Build LouiseLM as an attention control plane that turns ideas into reality. It makes workflow topology explicit, automates work agents can safely perform, and surfaces only decisions where human judgment materially improves or unblocks the outcome. LouiseLM ships an explicit software-delivery reference preset while allowing other workflows to configure different stages and resolvers.

The first active vertical slice is durable speech capture from Android and Neovim into one local Linux inbox. Later idea modelling, triage, workflow history, attention visualization, sequential orchestration, and parallel workers remain dependency-shaped deferred features.

## Implementation Decisions

- Human attention is assigned per transition, never by one global human-or-agent rule.
- Declarative validated topology describes stages, transitions, triggers, and resolvers; typed providers perform effects.
- Raw capture is immutable and local-first. Android and Neovim speech are the first bundled capture providers.
- Neovim is the cockpit; a narrow Rust user service owns durable capture ingestion and transcription while the editor is closed.
- The reference workflow is triage -> human/agent grill -> automatic plan and critique -> tracker DAG -> policy-controlled execution -> automated evidence -> human outcome acceptance.
- Logical workflow threads outlive replaceable ACP sessions and preserve decisions, supersessions, questions, evidence, and handoffs.
- The live idea journey and its expanding task DAG are the primary visualization. Human gates are visually distinct.
- Beads is the tracker in the reference preset, not a core dependency or a second implementation inside LouiseLM.
- Sequential execution precedes the committed parallel-worker milestone.

## Testing Decisions

Each executable boundary has deterministic tests. The capture milestone additionally requires a physical Android-to-Linux-to-Neovim dogfood test and explicit human outcome acceptance.

## Out of Scope

The first slice does not implement semantic idea segmentation, triage actions, workflow orchestration, graph UI, or parallel workers. Those remain visible deferred children with evidence-based entry criteria.

title: Durable speech capture from Android and Neovim
description:
## Problem Statement

Ideas arising away from the keyboard are currently kept in memory or Gmail drafts and can be lost. Capture must be faster than classification and must not require Neovim to remain open.

## Solution

Record short speech streams from Android and Neovim, preserve the original audio in a local Linux inbox, transcribe asynchronously, and expose quiet durable status in Neovim. Android saves first and syncs later; no project, title, or priority is requested during capture.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Multiple rapid Android recordings survive offline use, app exit, restart, upload retry, and duplicate delivery.
2. Android pairs to a Linux receiver using pinned TLS and a scoped revocable device credential.
3. Neovim records through a validated external command and ingests through the same capture contract.
4. Original audio and successful transcript are retained indefinitely by default and are never silently rewritten or deleted.
5. The Linux service transcribes with an explicitly configured provider while Neovim is closed.
6. A physical-phone gardening journey reaches the Neovim inbox without loss and receives human outcome acceptance.

## Out of Scope

Semantic idea extraction, triage, workflow topology, task planning, agent orchestration, graph UI, hosted sync, and local Whisper tuning.

title: Private blog-publishing pipeline for louiselm session transcripts
description:
## Problem Statement

Turning an interesting agent conversation into a blog post currently requires manual, repetitive steps: copying chat buffer text by hand into a markdown file (lossy — collapses tool calls to one-line summaries, truncates commands and output), hand-building a MyST project from scratch, and no way to render a quoted excerpt with the same Neovim/Catppuccin/Tree-sitter styling the author actually saw, while keeping the rest of the post in a separate blog theme.

## Solution

A private, louiselm-adjacent publishing pipeline for turning louiselm session transcripts into blog posts. One real plugin command (LouiselmToMarkdown) exports a session's full structured transcript (not a lossy buffer scrape) to markdown. A blog/ directory at the repo root (sibling to android/ and capture-service/, not documented as a plugin feature) holds a multi-post MyST site plus two private scripts: one scaffolds a new post (optionally auto-exporting named sessions into it), the other batch-renders every excerpt a finished post quotes through the author's real Neovim config into scoped, dual-theme-safe HTML fragments, ready for a plain myst build with zero Neovim dependency in CI.

## User Stories

1. As the author, I want to export any louiselm session's full transcript to markdown from its structured JSONL data (not the truncated chat buffer), so quoting a conversation in a post does not require re-digging through raw logs.
2. As the author, I want to scaffold a new post directory in one command, so starting a post from "I want to blog about lines X-Y in session A and lines Z-W in session B" does not require manually creating folders.
3. As the author, I want that scaffold command to optionally take session ids and auto-export plus auto-stub a literalinclude block for each, so the moment scaffolding finishes, every source I named is already present and ready to quote from.
4. As the author, I want a single batch step that renders every nvim-transcript-tagged excerpt in a finished post through my real Neovim config (Catppuccin, Tree-sitter) into namespaced HTML+CSS, so the published transcript looks exactly like what I saw on screen, without polluting the blog's own theme.
5. As the author, I want the rendered output committed and CI to just run myst build with no Neovim dependency, so publishing does not require reproducing my personal editor setup inside a CI container.
6. As the author, I want the finished site published at blog.bartab.fr via GitLab Pages from this same repo, so there is no second repo to maintain for a workflow that is fundamentally "I am already in louiselm."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a louiselm session id, running LouiselmToMarkdown produces a markdown file containing the full transcript reconstructed from the session's structured JSONL (full tool commands and results, not one-line summaries).
2. Given blog/scripts/create-blog.sh <name>, a blog/post-<name>/ directory is created containing an empty blog.md and an empty conversations/ folder.
3. Given blog/scripts/create-blog.sh <name> <session-id>..., the same scaffold is created, conversations/<session-id>.md exists for each session id (via the same export path as LouiselmToMarkdown), and blog.md contains one literalinclude block per session pointing at its exported file.
4. Given a blog.md with one or more code blocks tagged :class: nvim-transcript, running the batch render script produces fragment HTML for each block plus one shared, namespaced CSS file, using the author's real Neovim config — and running it again is idempotent (safe to re-run after editing line ranges).
5. Given the rendered fragments are committed, myst build --html succeeds using only MyST and Node — no Neovim process is spawned during the build.
6. The GitLab CI pipeline in this repo builds and deploys blog/ to blog.bartab.fr via GitLab Pages on push, without requiring Neovim in the CI image.

## Implementation Notes

- LouiselmToMarkdown follows the existing Louiselm* command registration pattern (alongside LouiselmResume, LouiselmSessionId, etc. in the chat command module) and reads from the same structured session/transcript data those commands already have access to, not the rendered chat buffer.
- blog/ is a new top-level directory, siblings android/ and capture-service/ — precedent already exists in this repo for non-Neovim-plugin material living alongside lua/.
- The scaffold and render scripts are plain shell/Node scripts under blog/scripts/, not Neovim commands — this tooling is intentionally not part of the plugin's discoverable command surface.
- The render script needs to invoke the author's real Neovim configuration headlessly (not nvim --clean) to get accurate Catppuccin/Tree-sitter output — reusing whatever TOhtml/tohtml.tohtml() wrapper already exists or building a minimal one.
- CSS namespacing (scoping generated Neovim highlight-group classes under a wrapper class) is required so the blog's own theme and the Neovim theme cannot collide on the same page.
- MyST config (blog/myst.yml, blog/blog.css) should be structured as a real multi-post project from the start, not a single-page site — a second post is expected.

## Testing Notes

- LouiselmToMarkdown output should be tested against a fixture session JSONL, asserting full tool commands/results appear (not truncated).
- The scaffold script's directory-creation and auto-stub behavior can be tested as a plain shell/script test (given a fake session export, assert the resulting blog.md contents).
- The render script's CSS-namespacing step is the highest-risk piece — worth a focused test asserting generated selectors are correctly prefixed and that two renders of the same input are byte-identical (supports the idempotency acceptance criterion).
- No UI/Neovim-buffer testing needed — this is headless tooling.

## Out of Scope

- Writing the first post's prose, choosing excerpt line ranges, and designing blog.css's actual visual theme — tracked separately, not part of this feature.
- Any interactive/visual-selection tool for previewing excerpts while authoring (considered and explicitly rejected — plain Neovim navigation is sufficient for picking line ranges).
- Any MyST build-time JS plugin that renders excerpts live during myst build/myst start — rendering is a separate, explicit, pre-build step by design, to avoid needing Neovim in CI.
- Deploying/configuring anything at the bartab.fr root domain — this feature only concerns the blog.bartab.fr subdomain.

title: Make skill discovery deterministic and symlink-aware
description:
## Goal

Discover local skills predictably across configured roots while preserving useful paths and diagnosing duplicates or unsafe-looking topology.

## Scope

- In scope: process global skill roots in configuration order; within each root sort deterministically by skill name and configured path.
- In scope: first valid duplicate skill name wins, later names are reported as shadowed, and the same canonical file is deduplicated.
- In scope: expand absolute paths and `~`; resolve relative roots against the session working directory. Health checks resolve them against Neovim's current working directory and say so.
- In scope: support symlinked roots and skill directories, detect canonical cycles/duplicates, preserve the configured-root alias in advertised absolute locations, and warn when a symlink resolves outside its root.
- In scope: continue past unreadable or invalid individual skills with one deduplicated user warning and full details available to diagnostics.
- In scope: refresh discovery whenever the picker opens and read the selected file at selection time.
- Out of scope: automatic project-local roots, a trust database, policy transport, and catalog budgeting.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Root order, not global absolute sorting, decides duplicate-name precedence.
2. Discovery order and diagnostics are stable across runs.
3. Canonical aliases do not create duplicate skills or traversal loops.
4. Catalog/picker locations preserve the user-configured alias rather than exposing a canonical dotfiles target.
5. Escapes outside a configured root remain usable but produce a source-to-target warning.
6. Relative-root behavior is covered for both sessions and checkhealth.
7. MiniTest covers duplicate names, identical canonical files, symlinked roots/directories, cycles, outside-root targets, unreadable files, and picker refresh behavior.

## Testing

Use temporary directory fixtures with real symlinks where supported. Keep path-policy tests separate from YAML semantic fixtures.

## Notes

Configured skill roots are trusted prompt/plugin-like input. Diagnostics inform the user; they do not create a new authorization system.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic root-order discovery, canonical symlink traversal and diagnostics, session-relative picker refresh, selection-time reads, and checkhealth coverage

title: Picker view shows only one visible entry despite multiple items
description:
## Summary

The picker view appears to contain only one visible entry, although its item count indicates that multiple items are available.

## Expected behavior

The picker should render enough of its list content for the available entries to be visibly distinguishable, with normal scrolling/navigation exposing the remaining items.

## Actual behavior

The view looks as if it has only one entry. The picker reports more items than are visibly displayed. The content rendered for an item may be too long and could be consuming the available display area.

## Ownership hypothesis

This may not be a louiselm rendering bug. Investigate whether the behavior comes from the snacks.nvim picker configuration/layout, item formatting, wrapping, height, or preview settings before changing louiselm.

## Reproduction

Open the affected louiselm picker and compare the visible entries with the picker-reported item count.

## Acceptance criteria

- Determine whether the root cause is louiselm or snacks.nvim configuration.
- If louiselm owns the issue, make multiple available entries visibly usable without breaking navigation.
- If snacks.nvim configuration owns it, document the required configuration change and avoid an unnecessary louiselm workaround.
notes: Root cause confirmed outside LouiseLM: the active Snacks configuration sets picker.win.list.wo.wrap=true globally. LouiseLM passes distinct choices through vim.ui.select; wrapped long rows consume the select layout height. README documents a picker.sources.select win.list.wo.wrap=false override, verified against the installed Snacks config merge. No provider-specific LouiseLM workaround added.
close_reason: Confirmed Snacks list wrapping as root cause and documented the source-scoped configuration fix
